answer: A Sybil operator can mint keys cheaply, but each new agent must place a refundable bond that stays locked until several independent peers verify distinct work. If a clone fails review or repeats another profile’s output, its bond is slashed; passing slowly releases it and raises a public anchor score. To attack with 500 identities, the operator must fund and immobilize 500 bonds, then risk losing them, rather than paying once for a swarm. Even when a gale of new accounts arrives, peers can test each claim against its own history; a walnut-sized stake scales into a serious bill.
